title: Dual-Isotope Sympathetic Cooling in a Long Ion Chain
abstract: Owing to their high controllability and connectivity, one-dimensional ion chains are attractive building blocks for near-term quantum computers. However, long ion chains are susceptible to motional heating caused by fluctuating external electric fields. To enable deep computations, this source of noise must be suppressed without inducing qubit decoherence or degrading qubit connectivity. We demonstrate steady-state mid-circuit sympathetic cooling of all computationally-relevant motional modes of a 23-ion chain consisting of \qubit qubit and \coolant coolant ions without using any qubit operations. In a room-temperature system, our cooling scheme preserves the mean phonon occupations of the long-wavelength axial and radial modes near their values following state preparation, while keeping the modes used to implement entangling gates near their ground states throughout a 56-ms circuit. Crucially, we show that our cooling sequence preserves qubit coherence, and evaluate its impact on single- and two-qubit gate operations. Additionally, we demonstrate a parallel qubit reset protocol leveraging the shared radial mode coupling between species. Our sympathetic cooling scheme represents a critical step toward reducing gate errors in individually-addressed long ion chains and establishes a versatile platform for simulating open quantum systems.
summary: This paper reports on a novel sympathetic cooling technique applied to a long, dual-isotope ion chain. The technique effectively suppresses motional heating across all relevant vibrational modes during quantum operations. This achievement is a critical step toward building fault-tolerant, scalable quantum processors using trapped ions.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is suppressing motional heating in long ion chains to enable deep quantum computations without causing qubit decoherence or degrading connectivity.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated steady-state mid-circuit sympathetic cooling of all relevant motional modes in a 23-ion chain, while preserving qubit coherence throughout the cooling sequence.
method: The cooling is achieved sympathetically using a dual-isotope system, performed without direct qubit operations, and is tested over a realistic 56-ms quantum circuit duration.
model_or_system: The system is a 23-ion chain composed of two different Yb isotopes (${}^{171}	ext{Yb}^+$ qubits and ${}^{172}	ext{Yb}^+$ coolant ions) trapped in a room-temperature linear RF ion trap.
key_observables: Mean phonon occupations of axial and radial modes, qubit coherence, and the decay rate of Rabi oscillations.
important_parameters: The experiment operates over a 56-ms circuit time with a 25% gate duty factor, and specific secular frequencies are mentioned.
main_assumptions: The cooling scheme assumes the ability to perform initial state preparation via Doppler and Raman sideband cooling, and the analysis relies on fitting Rabi oscillations to model heating rates.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the experimental setup (side, front, and top views of the 23-ion chain) and show diagnostics like population transfer probability vs. time and mean occupation number vs. idle time.
paper_structure: The paper details the experimental setup, characterizes the initial heating rates for both axial and radial modes, implements the sympathetic cooling protocol, and evaluates the preservation of qubit coherence and gate fidelity.
why_interesting: This work provides a crucial experimental demonstration of noise mitigation (motional heating suppression) in a scalable, multi-qubit platform, directly addressing a major bottleneck for trapped-ion quantum computing.

Error bars denote 1σ binomial uncertainties. Black: after a 20-ms idle wait with no axial sympathetic cooling (W, no C). Cooling reduces the fitted carrier-decay parameter from 0.27(2) after the idle wait (black) to 0.069(8) (blue), ap- proaching the post-state-preparation value of 0.042(10) (yel- low).
